slot.brief: Given a binomial situation with P(X = r) related to P(X = r+1) by a ratio, recover n or p, then compute another probability; 4/5.

stem: A random variable $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)$ has mean $4$ and satisfies $P(X=3)=2P(X=2)$. Find $P(X=4)$.

verdicts.working: Since \(np=4\), the ratio \(P(X=3)/P(X=2)=\frac{n-2}{3}\frac{p}{1-p}=2\) gives \((n-2)p=6(1-p)\). Substituting \(np=4\) yields \(p=\tfrac12\), so \(n=8\). Thus \(P(X=4)=\binom84(\tfrac12)^8=\tfrac{35}{128}\).

working:
$np=4,\quad\dfrac{P(X=3)}{P(X=2)}=\dfrac{n-2}{3}\dfrac{p}{1-p}=2.$ Substituting $p=\dfrac{4}{n}$ gives $n=8$, $p=\dfrac12$. $P(X=4)=\binom84\left(\dfrac12\right)^8=\dfrac{35}{128}$.

Independent check: Since \(np=4\), the ratio \(P(X=3)/P(X=2)=\frac{n-2}{3}\frac{p}{1-p}=2\) gives \((n-2)p=6(1-p)\). Substituting \(np=4\) yields \(p=\tfrac12\), so \(n=8\). Thus \(P(X=4)=\binom84(\tfrac12)^8=\tfrac{35}{128}\).
